records.title: Recognize emergencies and prepare transport
records.summary: See module decision boundaries; pain, illness or distress supersedes obedience. Emergency list is not exhaustive.
records.body: # Supreme Canine Academy — Canine care and life-stage planning Private review draft • 2026-11-01 • General education, observation and veterinary referral support, not diagnosis, treatment or a validated clinical resource. Seven modules supplement the training and nutrition collections; they do not replace either. Original planning worksheets below are editorial proposals, not tested clinical instruments. Source identities and claim provenance are maintained separately. **Training language throughout:** YES ends the position and promises a treat; GOOD means remain in position with reward later; NO means stop unwanted behavior; NOPE means adjust an incorrect playful teaching attempt; OKAY is general release. Positional commands imply holding until release or another command. Pain, fear, illness, exhaustion and urgent care are not obedience failures. Never use this cue system to compel a distressed dog to tolerate care. ## EDU-000507 — Recognize emergencies and prepare transport ### Purpose and immediate decision boundary Major breathing difficulty, collapse/unresponsiveness, severe bleeding, suspected poisoning or serious trauma require immediate veterinary contact and urgent care. Heavy panting with weakness, confusion or collapse after heat exposure is also urgent. This is not an exhaustive triage list. If uncertain whether a situation is an emergency, call a veterinary emergency service now rather than wait for an AI diagnosis. Call ahead when possible so the hospital can prepare. Do not delay departure to complete a worksheet. ### Prepare before an emergency Keep an offline card with the regular clinic and a currently verified emergency hospital: telephone, address, opening/receiving arrangements and route. Confirm that the facility handles dogs and identify a backup. Store the dog's identification, important conditions, current medications and caregiver contacts where another adult can find them. Do not put sensitive records on a publicly visible tag. Choose an appropriate transport arrangement during ordinary healthy life and practice calm entry when suitable. Keep the route out of the home clear. Decide who will drive, who can call the hospital, who will care for other animals and how a large dog could be moved with professional guidance. A rehearsal should involve logistics, not simulated restraint of a frightened or injured dog. ### During the event Move people away from immediate hazards without placing yourself at risk. Injured or frightened animals may bite; do not put your face near the dog's mouth or improvise forceful restraint. Describe the actual signs and ask the receiving team how to move the dog safely. Do not muzzle a dog that is struggling to breathe or vomiting. Follow real-time veterinary instructions rather than attempting a procedure from this document. Provide location, signs, onset time, known exposure or injury and estimated arrival. For suspected poisoning, bring or photograph the packaging if readily available without delaying care; do not induce vomiting, give medication or use a home antidote unless directed by the veterinary professional managing the case. Record who provided instructions. A passenger can document safely; the driver must not type or film. ### Handoff and training boundary Give the receiving team a short sequence of events and what, if anything, was administered under instruction. Distinguish what was witnessed from what is suspected. Allow staff to triage; do not delay entry to obtain a better video or finish a training exercise. Normal reward, release and position routines are secondary to emergency care. **Q: Can the assistant rule out danger from a photo?** No. **Q: Should I wait until the dog responds to a cue?** No. **Q: Does this replace first-aid training?** No. Arrange practical veterinary-approved instruction separately; this module intentionally provides no CPR, dosing, wound-management or home-treatment recipe.

records.title: Urgent signs come before feeding advice
records.summary: Any listed emergency sign; this list is not exhaustive.
records.body: # Supreme Canine Academy ## Canine nutrition and feeding — review draft Version 0.1.0 • Evidence checked 2026-11-01 **Not clinically validated. Not a personalized diet, diagnosis or treatment plan.** This is a first education/triage module, not an exhaustive canine nutrition textbook. A veterinarian must review medical content before production use. ### How to use this draft Start with urgent signs. For a stable dog, identify the question, read the matching section, collect missing facts, and separate general education from a decision requiring veterinary review. Do not combine fragments into a personalized prescription. Each section is a retrieval unit; retain its referral trigger and draft status when indexing. ## NUT-001 — Urgent signs come before feeding advice Seek emergency veterinary care now for collapse, trouble breathing, seizures, severe or repeated vomiting, a painful swollen abdomen, repeated attempts to vomit without producing anything, or severe bloody diarrhea. Do not troubleshoot these as ordinary food preference or training problems. Repeated dry retching with restlessness or abdominal swelling can signal a rapidly life-threatening stomach emergency, even before collapse. For the assistant: lead with the urgent action, then ask only details that help the clinic. Do not delay care to complete a feeding questionnaire. No home treatment, forced feeding or diagnostic certainty is supplied here.

records.title: Read the nutritional adequacy statement
records.summary: Unclear adequacy or a medical condition requiring diet selection.
records.body: # Supreme Canine Academy ## Canine nutrition and feeding — review draft Version 0.1.0 • Evidence checked 2026-11-01 **Not clinically validated. Not a personalized diet, diagnosis or treatment plan.** This is a first education/triage module, not an exhaustive canine nutrition textbook. A veterinarian must review medical content before production use. ### How to use this draft Start with urgent signs. For a stable dog, identify the question, read the matching section, collect missing facts, and separate general education from a decision requiring veterinary review. Do not combine fragments into a personalized prescription. Each section is a retrieval unit; retain its referral trigger and draft status when indexing. ## NUT-002 — Read the nutritional adequacy statement The useful question is whether the food is intended to supply the whole diet for the relevant life stage—not whether the package looks premium. Find its nutritional adequacy statement. A complete-and-balanced claim can be supported by meeting an established nutrient profile or by feeding-test procedures. This does not mean the food suits every individual medical condition. Treats, snacks and supplements may not be adequate as the sole diet. Photograph the exact statement rather than guessing from the front label. If it is absent or unclear, request clarification before treating that product as the dog's main food.

Do not combine fragments into a personalized prescription. Each section is a retrieval unit; retain its referral trigger and draft status when indexing. ## NUT-003 — Match the label to the individual dog Record the intended species, life stage, feeding directions and energy information. A diet appropriate for adult maintenance is not automatically a suitable growth diet. A package feeding amount is a starting guide, not proof of an individual dog's needs. Compare the units carefully: a daily amount is different from an amount per meal. Reader worksheet: exact product and variety; adequacy wording; calories per gram or stated serving; amount actually offered; amount left; snacks; household members who feed. Keep product details in the dog's private record, not in fictional examples or public testimonials.

records.summary: Weight-management target missing; therapeutic diet; feeding restriction.
records.body: # Supreme Canine Academy ## Canine nutrition and feeding — review draft Version 0.1.0 • Evidence checked 2026-11-01 **Not clinically validated. Not a personalized diet, diagnosis or treatment plan.** This is a first education/triage module, not an exhaustive canine nutrition textbook. A veterinarian must review medical content before production use. ### How to use this draft Start with urgent signs. For a stable dog, identify the question, read the matching section, collect missing facts, and separate general education from a decision requiring veterinary review. Do not combine fragments into a personalized prescription. Each section is a retrieval unit; retain its referral trigger and draft status when indexing. ## NUT-004 — Build a complete daily food ledger For many healthy dogs, at least 90% of daily calories should come from the complete-and-balanced diet; noncomplete extras should generally stay at or below 10%. That is a ceiling, not a target. A medically prescribed diet may require stricter rules. Count training rewards, chews, table food and food used for medication. Use a veterinarian-agreed daily target rather than inventing one from breed alone. For arithmetic only, a fictional 600-calorie target gives a 60-calorie extras ceiling. Fifteen four-calorie rewards would use that entire ceiling. These numbers are not a recommendation for a real dog.

records.summary: Growth concern, poor intake, supplement proposal, pregnancy or nursing.
records.body: # Supreme Canine Academy ## Canine nutrition and feeding — review draft Version 0.1.0 • Evidence checked 2026-11-01 **Not clinically validated. Not a personalized diet, diagnosis or treatment plan.** This is a first education/triage module, not an exhaustive canine nutrition textbook. A veterinarian must review medical content before production use. ### How to use this draft Start with urgent signs. For a stable dog, identify the question, read the matching section, collect missing facts, and separate general education from a decision requiring veterinary review. Do not combine fragments into a personalized prescription. Each section is a retrieval unit; retain its referral trigger and draft status when indexing. ## NUT-006 — Puppies and growth need their own plan Use food appropriate for growth until skeletal maturity; the timing varies with expected adult size. Large and giant puppies need careful growth support, a lean body condition and avoidance of excessive calcium. Do not add calcium simply because a puppy is growing or expected to become large. Bring the growth record, exact food label, supplement list and expected adult size to veterinary review. Do not apply an adult weight-loss plan to a puppy. A single birthday is not enough information to choose the adult-diet switch date. Pregnancy and nursing also require a separately reviewed feeding plan.
